prompt: How do I use the chi squared goodness of fit test to show the correlation between the times of 5k collegiate runners and their altitude
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 is the only response that attempts to use a chi-squared goodness-of-fit workflow and explicitly frames hypotheses in terms of differences across altitude groups. However, it misapplies GOF logic by treating expected counts as N/k (effectively a uniform/unspecified expectation) and does not correctly set up chi-square testing to demonstrate association/correlation between time and altitude. Candidate 4 provides generic, mostly correct GOF procedure but stays focused on comparing observed data to an assumed distribution, not correlating altitude with times. Candidates 2 and 3 use other methods (ANOVA, correlation/regression) and therefore largely fail the specific “chi-squared GOF for correlation with altitude” requirement.
